title: Ukban the Babylonian
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman summarizes [Sanhedrin 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.31b.17) as follows. They sent word from the Land of Israel to Mar Ukva to make peace between Ukban and his brother Yirmiyah. If he would not listen to him, he was to persuade him to go to Tiberias. See there.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The linked letter addresses Mar Ukva and names Ukban the Babylonian as the complainant against his brother Yirmiyah. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2872&lang=en) also gives the two brothers and directs readers to Mar Ukva.
The condition “if he would not listen to him” is part of Hyman’s paraphrase.

[Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sanhedrin.31b.17.3-5) says that Yirmiyah was to be urged to reconcile and made to come to Tiberias for a hearing. Rashi gives two explanations of Ukban’s grievance, one involving physical injury and the other a financial dispute.
